title: GBL-134 dropped tenant_default copies of 4 tables (entity_definitions, entity_record_latest, entity_type_instances, artifact_activation_groups) that ISS-0185's own diagnosis classifies as PER_TENANT (canonical=tenant_default) -- unconditional DROP TABLE with no data-loss guard, already executed against bpm_test and bpm_dev
registered_by: ISSUE-FIXER (WF03-GH566-20260808, incidental finding while diagnosing GH-566/ISS-0617's tier-quota resolution failure)
related_to: ISS-0185 / GH #518 -- the run that introduced this migration (PR #569, merged 2026-08-08)

ISS-0617 / GH #566 -- the run during which this was discovered (a DIFFERENT, narrower gap in the same migration: 13 GLOBAL_REGISTRY tables it should have included but didn't, including repository_artifacts)
scope: migrations/GBL-134_iss0185_drop_global_registry_shadows.sql -- already executed against the shared bpm_test database and workspace r-co-2's bpm_dev database. Any other database this migration has been or will be applied to (other developer workspaces, any deployed environment) is equally affected.
symptom: migrations/GBL-134_iss0185_drop_global_registry_shadows.sql's v_tables allow-list (lines 45-70) includes 'artifact_activation_groups', 'entity_definitions', 'entity_record_latest', and 'entity_type_instances'. docs/issue-reports/ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml's own classification_table (lines 88-101, 'per_tenant_public_is_stray') lists these SAME 4 table names as PER_TENANT -- meaning tenant_default is supposed to be the CANONICAL copy and public the stray shadow, the OPPOSITE of what GBL-134 assumes. GBL-134 unconditionally executed 'DROP TABLE %I.%I RESTRICT' (line 107) against every tenant schema's copy of these 4 tables, with no row-count check, no emptiness guard, and no backup step. Confirmed via direct psql inspection: tenant_default.entity_definitions, tenant_default.entity_record_latest, tenant_default.entity_type_instances, and tenant_default.artifact_activation_groups no longer exist in bpm_test (only the public copies remain, currently 0 rows each in this particular database). schema_migrations confirms GBL-134 has also been applied to workspace r-co-2's bpm_dev database (applied_at 2026-08-08 05:44:11+00).
root_cause_analysis: The migration's own header comment (lines 18-21) claims 'GLOBAL (24): shadow in tenant_default must be dropped' as if this were the complete and verified GLOBAL set, and the migration's Safety Properties section (lines 23-33) explicitly asserts 'The shadow-name list below is the explicit allow-list of GLOBAL table names per the ISS-0185 classification' -- but this claim is factually wrong for at least these 4 names. The classification's own separately-computed method (docs/issue-reports/ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml lines 46-52: 'PER_TENANT = the table has a tenant_id column on at least one copy and the column shape is identical between schemas') independently placed these 4 tables in the PER_TENANT bucket, but whoever authored the v_tables array for GBL-134 either worked from a different/earlier draft of the classification, misread the two buckets, or manually curated the list without cross-checking against the diagnosis file's own final classification_table section. The safety comment's claim of verification (line 18: 'Classification (verified via pg_constraint + pg_depend queries)') describes a process that evidently did not catch this discrepancy, or was not actually re-run against the diagnosis file's final output before the migration was written.
impact: Any tenant_default row that existed in entity_definitions, entity_record_latest, entity_type_instances, or artifact_activation_groups and was not already separately present in the public copy is now unrecoverable via the schema alone (no application code creates a backup before this migration runs). In the shared bpm_test database, the remaining public copies of all 4 tables currently show 0 rows -- this does NOT prove no data was lost, only that whatever currently exists post-drop is empty; there is no record of row counts immediately before the drop. The same migration has also executed against workspace r-co-2's bpm_dev database. Any other environment (other developer workspaces' local databases, CI ephemeral databases that happened to be seeded with fixture data before this migration ran, or -- if this repository has any deployed/production database -- that database) that has applied or will apply this migration is equally exposed. This blocks any workflow that assumes tenant-scoped entity/artifact-activation data survives routine migrations, and is a genuine, already-executed data-loss event in at least two known databases.
acceptance_criteria: Immediately confirm the actual scope: which databases (this repo's shared test DB, both workspaces' dev DBs, any CI/deployed environment) have applied GBL-134, and for each, whether entity_definitions/entity_record_latest/entity_type_instances/artifact_activation_groups had any tenant_default rows at the time of the drop (check for available backups, WAL archives, or point-in-time-recovery options before concluding data is unrecoverable)

Correct the ISS-0185 classification and/or GBL-134's v_tables list so these 4 tables are removed from the GLOBAL_REGISTRY drop set -- and re-verify (do not re-trust) the remaining 24 GLOBAL_REGISTRY entries and the GBL-135 PER_TENANT entries against the diagnosis file's classification_table with a fresh, auditable cross-check, not a repeat of whatever process produced this discrepancy

If data loss is confirmed in any database that matters (not just an easily-reseeded local test DB), determine whether recovery is possible and execute it, or formally document the loss and its business impact

A forward-fix migration (not a rewrite of GBL-134, which has already run and cannot un-run itself) that recreates tenant_default.<table> for each of the 4 tables per tenant schema, going forward, so future tenant provisioning is not silently missing these tables
tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py (added by ISS-0185 to prevent future re-duplication) is checked to confirm it does not also encode this same 4-table misclassification
evidence_file: Confirmed via direct docker exec psql inspection during WF03-GH566-20260808 (2026-08-08): \dt tenant_default.entity_definitions / entity_record_latest / entity_type_instances / artifact_activation_groups all return 'Did not find any relation' against bpm_test; public copies exist with 0 rows each. schema_migrations on bpm_dev (r-co-2-db-1) confirms GBL-134 applied_at 2026-08-08T05:44:11Z.
notes: Discovered incidentally while diagnosing GH-566/ISS-0617 (a narrower, non-data-loss gap in the SAME migration -- 13 different GLOBAL_REGISTRY tables it should have included but didn't). This finding is more severe (BLOCKER, potential already-executed data loss) than ISS-0617 (MAJOR, a test-only-visible resolution bug) and is filed as its own issue rather than folded into ISS-0617's fix, per the incidental-discovery protocol. GH-566/ISS-0617's own work continues separately and is not blocked by this filing, since ISS-0617's fix does not touch GBL-134 or the 4 misclassified tables.
